news.title: WashU Racing drives to best finish in club history
news.summary_en: Members of WashU Racing commit more than 20 hours a week to building and testing a formula-style race car from scratch — six-hour building days, 12-hour testing days and dozens and dozens of meetings designing systems, planning logistics and finding sponsors. That work paid off this spring, when WashU Racing achieved its highest showing in club history at the annual Formula SAE competition.

news.title: Early-pregnancy air pollution exposure linked to persistent depressive symptoms
news.summary_en: WashU Bursky Public Health researchers found the first six weeks of pregnancy may be a particularly sensitive period.

news.title: Groves named inaugural Stuart A. Kornfeld Distinguished Professor
news.summary_en: Andrew K. Groves, a renowned developmental biologist known for his research into inner ear development and hearing loss with a focus on the potential for hearing restoration, has been named the inaugural Stuart A. Kornfeld Distinguished Professor of Medical Sciences at WashU Medicine.

news.title: Quick optical biopsy could be early detection method for endometrial cancer
news.summary_en: Biomedical engineer Quing Zhu and WashU Medicine collaborators combined optical coherence tomography and machine learning for a rapid, accurate test for endometrial cancer.

news.title: Rosengart named inaugural Theodore and Bertha Bryan Professor of Environmental Medicine
news.summary_en: Matthew R. Rosengart, MD, a leading expert on sepsis and circadian rhythms whose research has improved care and outcomes for vulnerable patients, has been installed as the inaugural Theodore and Bertha Bryan Professor of Environmental Medicine in the WashU Medicine Mary Culver Department of Surgery.

news.title: ‘Buenos Aires Modern, 1935–1950’
news.summary_en: The Kemper Art Museum at Washington University in St. Louis will present “Buenos Aires Modern, 1935–1950,” on view Sept. 9 to Jan. 4. This exhibition is the first in the United States to examine the inventive activities of a thriving, cross-disciplinary artistic community of locals, exiles and immigrants living in Buenos Aires during the early 20th century.

news.title: Commemorating 250 years of American independence
news.summary_en: As the nation prepares to celebrate the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence signing, experts at Washington University in St. Louis are reflecting on the events and ideas that shaped this nation and their continued relevance today.

news.title: Is the American Dream in serious trouble?
news.summary_en: Fewer than half of Americans, around 49%, believe that all people in this country have the ability to achieve the American Dream, according to a recent survey from the Public Religion Research Institute. Among those under age 30, it falls to 36%. This should serve as a wake-up call for all of us, says WashU’s Mark Rank.

news.title: Free speech and judicial independence in the age of revolution
news.summary_en: The right to free speech and judicial independence — two foundational values our nation is built upon — were born of the founders’ distrust of unchecked power, according to Andrew D. Martin, chancellor of Washington University in St. Louis and an expert in judicial politics.
